entities.text: Amit Kumar Mangal Vs State Of M.P
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: Shri Harshad Bahirani, learned counsel for the petitioner.
Shri Vikrant Sharma, learned PP for the respondent/State.

Counsel for the petitioner pressed for stay over proceedings of the trial Court as according to him,
trial Court is likely to pronounce the judgment soon.

Learned counsel for the State opposed the prayer by submitting that if trial Court is pronouncing the judgment then it would be in the fitness of things that judgment be passed finally as petitioner would have remedy of filing the appeal.

The present petition under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. has been preferred by the petitioner for quashment of criminal case No. 1016/2008 pending before JMFC, Vidisha under Section 2(i)7(1)
and 16(1)(a)(i) of the Prevention of Food Adulteration Act as well as for quashment of order dated 18/6/2008; whereby, cognizance has been taken by the trial Court.
Looking to the nature of controversy, prayer for interim relief deserves to be rejected.

However,
petitioner pressed the matter for hearing on merits but looking to the fact that matter is pending before the trial Court since June, 2008 i.e. for more than 11 years and petitioner was enjoying the stay granted vide order dated 27/6/2013, in light of the judgment passed by Apex Court in the matter of Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd. and Anr. Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation,
AIR 2018 SC 2039, the stay was impliedly vacated and therefore, petitioner prays for extension of interim order by filing I.A.No. 6484/2019 but in the fitness of things, looking to the pending case,

entities.text:
Asian Resurfacing of Road Agency Pvt. Ltd. and Anr. Vs. Central Bureau of Investigation,
AIR 2018 SC 2039
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: I.A. stands rejected.

So far as, plea of petitioner for hearing of matter on merits is concerned, it also deserve rejection on the ground that as per the submissions 2 MCRC-4766-2013 of counsel for the petitioner himself,
trial has been completed and matter is placed for pronouncement of judgment.
Perusal of order dated 27/6/2013 passed by this Court also indicates that proceedings of trial Court were directed to be continued and passing of final order was stayed.
Petitioner was enjoying the stay order for last six years and if the stay would have been granted then it would have given the petitioner again a fresh lease of life for some years,

sentences.text: 1 Court is likely to pronounce the judgment then hearing of the case on merits would preempt the controversy and when parties had the chance to lead evidence, then at this juncture on technical pretext, hearing of petition filed under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. would amount to exceeding the extraordinary jurisdiction vested in this Court.

Hon'ble Apex Court time and again has cautioned regarding the scope of interference under extraordinary jurisdiction vested under Section 482 of Cr.P.C. and when trial is at the fag end and judgment is likely to be pronounced soon then no purpose exists for keeping the petition pending.
Thus, petition is disposed of with direction to the trial Court to proceed with the trial and pronounce the judgment in accordance with law.
Needless to say that parties must have advanced their arguments as per law and trial Court shall take care of those arguments which were advanced by the parties before it.
Petition stands disposed of with the aforesaid direction.
A copy of this order be sent to concerned trial Court immediately for information and compliance.

(ANAND PATHAK) JUDGE JPS/-
JAI PRAKASH SOLANKI 2019.09.17 18:11:19 +05'30'
